_citation: Buie, M. W., Grundy, W. M., Young, E. F., Young, L. A. & Stern, S. A. (2010), 'Pluto and Charon with the Hubble Space Telescope. I. Monitoring global change and improved surface properties from light curves', Astronomical Journal 139, 1117-1127. DOI:10.1088/0004-6256/139/3/1117.
_transcription: Transcribed by hand from the published PDF. HST ACS/HRC photometry 2002 June - 2003 June, Pluto and Charon resolved, transformed to Johnson B and V (F435W, F555W; Sec. 3.3). Magnitudes are 'corrected to mean opposition distance (r = 39.5 AU and Delta = 38.5 AU)' (Sec. 3.3, p. 1120).

pluto.V_a0_1deg_source: Table 8 (p. 1122), n=0 Fourier term: mean V light curve at 1 deg phase
pluto.V_to_zero_phase_source: Fig. 2 caption (p. 1122): 'Subtract 0.0398 mag to correct the new data to 0 deg phase angle' (Hapke fit, Table 9)
pluto.beta_source: Abstract and Sec. 5.2 (p. 1122): linear phase coefficients from the F555W and F435W data

charon.B_minus_V_source: Table 10 (p. 1123), weighted mean; also the abstract. Sec. 6.3 prints 0.7313 +- 0.0017 as the adopted value
charon.phase_range_source: Abstract: solar phase angle 0.36-1.74 deg (Pluto and Charon observed together)

hapke_table9._source: Table 9 (p. 1123), 'Global Hapke Parameters'. Columns h, P(g), B0, theta (roughness, deg; [x] = held fixed), chi2, w. Radii used: Pluto 1153 km, Charon 606 km.
